# A comment after closing brackets that are on a line of their own is kept.
# It is written after the last element or argument in the brackets, which is
# not where it was. That is a compromise, since the AST does not say where
# closing brackets are; the want files show the current output, not the
# intended one. See closerComment in format.go.
celfmt -i call.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_call.txt

celfmt -i nested.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout nested.cel

celfmt -i map.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_map.txt

# Lines of closing brackets without a comment are passed over.
celfmt -i stacked.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_stacked.txt

# The comment is kept when the result is formatted again.
celfmt -i want_branch.txt
! stderr .
stdout '\) // c5'

celfmt -i branch.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_branch.txt

-- call.cel --
size(
	state.x
) // c1
-- want_call.txt --
size(
	state.x // c1
)
-- nested.cel --
state.x.as(y,
	y.z.as(w,
		w + 1 // c2
	) // c3
)
-- map.cel --
{
	"a": {
		"b": 1,
	}, // c4
}
-- want_map.txt --
{
	"a": {
		"b": 1, // c4
	},
}
-- branch.cel --
state.a ?
	(state.b &&
	state.e) // c5
:
	state.d
-- want_branch.txt --
state.a ?
	(
		state.b && state.e
	) // c5
:
	state.d
-- stacked.cel --
state.x.with(
	state.y.with(
		state.z
	)
) // c6
-- want_stacked.txt --
state.x.with(
	state.y.with(
		state.z // c6
	)
)
